# Semantic Breaks

This page describes how the core plugin `claudetto` puts each sentence of a Markdown file on its own line.
It is for a user who writes Markdown with Claude and for a contributor who edits the `sembr` slice.

## What It Does

A `tool.call` hook rewrites the `Write` and `Edit` calls for a Markdown file.
It also rewrites the quoted heredoc of `git commit` and `gh pr create` in a `Bash` call.
Each sentence starts on a new line, and a long sentence breaks only between clauses.
The hook never breaks a line at a column or in a word.

## How It Finds a Sentence End

The hook uses `Intl.Segmenter` with sentence granularity and the locale `und`.
These are the Unicode sentence rules with CLDR data.
They work for each written language, for example Polish, Russian, and Japanese (`。`).
The hook has no word list of abbreviations and no rule about capital letters.
A break can follow an abbreviation, such as `np.` or `e.g.`, when a capital letter follows it.
This only moves the text to a new line, and Markdown shows the same paragraph.
If the runtime has no `Intl.Segmenter`, the hook makes no break.

## What It Keeps

The hook leaves code blocks, inline code, tables, and links as they are.
A list item and a quote keep their prefix on each new line, so a break stays inside the item or the quote.
A file with CRLF line ends keeps CRLF on each line that the hook writes.

An `Edit` call whose `old_string` crosses a sentence break is split to match the file.
The hook runs before the guards, so the guards see the rewritten call.
